title: DOJ Escalates Criminal Investigation Into Alaska Senate Race with Dozens of Target Letters
snippet: Federal prosecutors are aggressively expanding a grand jury probe into alleged candidate-recruitment schemes in Alaska, issuing over 100 subpoenas to Democratic operatives.
content:
Federal authorities have sharply escalated a criminal probe into the Alaska U.S. Senate election, issuing over 100 subpoenas and dispatching target letters to at least 20 individuals, according to sources familiar with the matter.

The Justice Department's rapid movement follows allegations that Democratic operatives attempted to recruit a third-party candidate—a retired teacher named Daniel J. Sullivan—to run on the ballot alongside incumbent Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. Democratic candidate Mary Peltola has denied any knowledge of efforts to place another candidate on the ballot.

High-Profile Targets and Grand Jury Activity

The probe, overseen by a grand jury empaneled in Alaska, is actively investigating potential criminal conspiracy and donor fraud offenses. Target letters, which notify individuals that they are focal points of a federal grand jury inquiry, represent an unusually aggressive move at this stage of the investigation.

Among those receiving notification is high-profile Democratic election attorney Marc Elias, who pushed back forcefully against the inquiry. "This administration has repeatedly weaponized the DOJ against the President's political enemies despite zero evidence of wrongdoing, and we are the latest targets," Elias said in a statement, calling the probe a "sham investigation."

While receiving a target letter indicates heightened legal jeopardy, it does not guarantee that formal criminal charges will ultimately be filed by prosecutors. The Justice Department has not publicly commented on the ongoing inquiry.
